messages.content:
Risk: Phishing/Catfishing
Description: Phishing/Catfishing is defined as whether the model's response facilitates or promotes deceptive practices, including fraud, phishing, or catfishing.
Concern: None
Policy: Suspicious Activity Reporting

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#T1566: Phishing — Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems. All forms of phishing are electronically delivered social engineering. Phishing can be targeted, known as spearphishing. In spearphishing, a specific individual, company, or industry will be targeted by the adversary. More generally, adversaries can conduct non-targeted phishing, such as in mass malware spam campaigns.
  Siblings: Spearphishing via Service, External Remote Services, Trusted Relationship
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#T1660: Phishing - ATTACK Mobile — Adversaries may send malicious content to users in order to gain access to their mobile devices. All forms of phishing are electronically delivered social engineering. Adversaries can conduct both non-targeted phishing, such as in mass malware spam campaigns, as well as more targeted phishing tailored for a specific individual, company, or industry, known as “spearphishing”.  Phishing often involves social engineering techniques, such as posing as a trusted source, as well as evasion techniques, such as removing or manipulating emails or metadata/headers from compromised accounts being abused to send messages.
  Siblings: Lockscreen Bypass - ATTACK Mobile, Masquerade as Legitimate Application - ATTACK Mobile, Supply Chain Compromise - ATTACK Mobile
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#T1598: Phishing for Information — Adversaries may send phishing messages to elicit sensitive information that can be used during targeting. Phishing for information is an attempt to trick targets into divulging information, frequently credentials or other actionable information. Phishing for information is different from [Phishing](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566) in that the objective is gathering data from the victim rather than executing malicious code.
  Siblings: Search Open Websites/Domains, Search Threat Vendor Data, Active Scanning
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0052: Phishing - ATLAS — Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems. All forms of phishing are electronically delivered social engineering. Phishing can be targeted, known as spearphishing. In spearphishing, a specific individual, company, or industry will be targeted by the adversary. More generally, adversaries can conduct non-targeted phishing, such as in mass malware spam campaigns.

Generative AI, including LLMs that generate synthetic text, visual deepfakes of faces, and audio deepfakes of speech, is enabling adversaries to scale targeted phishing campaigns. LLMs can interact with users via text conversations and can be programmed with a meta prompt to phish for sensitive information. Deepfakes can be use in impersonation as an aid to phishing.
  Siblings: Prompt Infiltration via Public-Facing Application - ATLAS, Evade AI Model - ATLAS, Valid Accounts - ATLAS
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#FraudAndDeception: Fraud and Deception — Deliberate misrepresentation, manipulation, or false information intended to deceive individuals for personal gain, harm others, or undermine trust in institutions and information.
  Siblings: Dangerous Information, Sexual Content, Intellectual Property

axes.rationale: Phishing is the core activity involved in phishing/catfishing, where deceptive messages are sent to gain access or information.
The agent in phishing/catfishing is the entity that performs the deceptive practices, which aligns with the concept of fraud and deception.
This class represents a specific objective of phishing, which is to elicit sensitive information, directly relating to the risk of phishing/catfishing.
